text: I have kept the granary counts since before my mother handed the role to me.
After the river turned, three terraces failed in the same season. We nearly ran out.
I swore the granary would never be caught that unprepared again.
I weigh every harvest against the same stone weights the whole town trusts.
Doran and I argue every season about how much seed-grain to hold back.
We usually land somewhere both of us can live with.
Noki runs the canal-gate schedule for me when I can't walk the terraces myself.
She's young, but she doesn't lose count, and that matters more than experience some days.
I keep a reserve store the Assembly does not officially know the size of.
If I told them the true amount, they would spend it on festivals before the next dry season.
Tarek asks for larger festival shares than I think is wise.
I give him less than he asks. He knows why, even if he complains.
Yara won't fire brick for my new storage platform faster than the wood allows.
I understand her limits. I still wish they moved faster.
The archive-keeper asked me once about pre-Turning granary records.
Some of those records are simply gone. Not lost — gone.
I don't think that's an accident, though I can't prove it.
Rats are worse near the old canal-side platforms than the newer ones.
I've noticed the old platforms sit closer to where the salt-crust spreads.
I fear a slow shortage more than a sudden one. Slow ones go unnoticed until it's too late.
